explanation.definitionFit: Smocks and shifts are both loose, simple garments, the shift being a plain dress or chemise.

clue.text: Item worn in shower by son of king?

K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.definitionFit: A mack is a raincoat, the garment you put on to go out in a rain shower.

clue.text: Well-known person managed time to see vicar at wedding?

ran a business means managed it

explanation.surface: A famous person ran late to catch sight of the clergyman at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrant is the priest who officiates at a ceremony, such as a vicar conducting a marriage service.

clue.text: Line under Paris going round winding curve

going round suggests the letters of the city's name being spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A Metro line beneath Paris circles round on a twisting route.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral is a curve that winds continually around a central point.

clue.text: Doctor does feel it's suicide

explanation.surface: A medic feels that a death was self-inflicted.
explanation.walkthrough: FELO DE SE is a Latin legal term, literally a felon of himself, for someone who takes their own life.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal phrase names self-murder, the old crime of killing oneself.

clue.text: Bodice theft? Moon may provide aid in search

clue.text: Transparency showing girl embrace unloved ass

parts.note: an ass is a fool, an idiot

explanation.surface: A clear statement: a girl hugs a donkey nobody cares for.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucidity is clearness, of water or of expression, the quality of being transparent.

clue.text: Divine duo two-step regularly

indicators.note: regularly means take letters at regular intervals, here every other one starting with the first

explanation.surface: A pair of dancers performs a two-step beautifully.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to search for water with a rod, which is also called divining.

clue.text: Seconds left to use four-letter word for polo shirts?

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a four-letter word is a swear word, so using one is to swear

explanation.definitionFit: Polo shirts are an example of casual athletic clothing; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Young family member's eaten the whole salad plant

parts.note: a scion is a young descendant of a family
the whole means all

explanation.surface: A child in the family has polished off an entire salad.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallion is a spring onion, eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Production of a crowd scene in the 17 18

indicators.note: a production of these letters remakes them into a new order

explanation.surface: Staging a crowd scene in a famous Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: The 17 18 is the Scottish Play, Macbeth; Macbeth is Thane of Cawdor and scenes are set at Cawdor castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cawdor is a setting in the tragedy, the castle of the thane whose title the hero receives.

clue.text: Largely insouciant band leader causing scene in the 17 18

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: blasé means unconcerned, insouciant
Ted Heath was a famous British big-band leader

explanation.surface: A casual bandleader creates a scene during the play.
explanation.walkthrough: The British reader may think first of the prime minister Edward Heath, but this Ted Heath led a well-known dance band from the 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: The witches first meet Macbeth on a blasted heath, a barren moor, in the play.

clue.text: From text I see you solve last of down clues to begin with — oddly decisive!

indicators.note: to begin with takes the opening letter of clues
oddly signals that the gathered letters are shuffled into a strange order

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of down

explanation.surface: A text message says I see you have solved the down clues, which proves decisive.
explanation.walkthrough: From text points to text-speak, where see you is CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Conclusive evidence settles a question, so it is decisive.

clue.text: Starts to complain of mild alcoholic stupor

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A drinker begins grumbling about a weak drink causing a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: A coma is a deep state of unconsciousness, the extreme form of stupor.

clue.text: What the larger person has done wrong?

definitions.text: What the larger person has done

parts.note: the reading treats OUT as an anagram signal applied to GROWN, which rearranged makes the clue's word wrong

explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards as a clue, the answer splits as OUT (an anagram signal) and GROWN, whose letters jumbled spell the clue word wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who has become bigger than their clothes has outgrown them.

clue.text: By all accounts, theatre's given us the odd topless 18 periodically

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

parts.note: 18 is the answer at 18-across, a drama; topless means without its first letter, leaving a word meaning set down

explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes alternate letters from 'us the odd' plus LAY, the 18 PLAY with its top removed, giving UTEDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputedly means according to what people say, the same as by all accounts.

clue.text: Setter has opossum running round more quickly

running suggests the animal's letters moving about into a new order

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.definitionFit: Più mosso is an Italian musical direction meaning play with more movement, faster.

clue.text: A 26 almost lost it badly, having said 2 22

almost means drop the last letter

explanation.walkthrough: 2 22 is MACK BETH, which spoken sounds like Macbeth: theatre superstition has actors call it this instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The superstitious nickname actors use in place of the title of Shakespeare's tragedy of Macbeth.

clue.text: See 17
Cost of maintaining prince in posh part of castle

the keep is the strongest tower of a castle

explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the expense of maintaining a building or property in good repair.

clue.text: Female rook's deserted sleeping place

parts.note: a berth is a bed on a ship or train
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of each of the two words

explanation.definitionFit: Midges are tiny biting insects, small flies.

clue.text: Ignored the "Micawber principle", so failed as an artist?

explanation.walkthrough: Mr Micawber, from David Copperfield, said income twenty pounds and expenditure nineteen means happiness; one more pound means misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdrawing an account means taking out more money than it holds; split, the word is drawing too much.
